links.comparator_used: Base model (off-the-shelf recogniser) under identical preprocessing, on held-out reports
links.outcome: Laboratory value reading accuracy on held-out reports
links.effect: Fine-tuned model lost 8.1 percentage points against its base model (unadjusted p = 0.031). It read its tuning document perfectly at low resolution. It was the most accurate reader on one half of the held-out set and the least accurate on the other.
links.tradeoff: The aggregate loss hid a reversal across the two halves of the held-out set. The result does not survive correction for multiple testing.
links.quote: Fine-tuning the recogniser did not help: it read the document it was tuned for perfectly at low resolution, but against its own base model under identical preprocessing it lost 8.1 percentage points on held-out reports (unadjusted p = 0.031; this and the corresponding version 1 comparison do not survive correction for multiple testing).

links.comparator_used: Same pages without upscaling before recognition (same model)
links.outcome: Value reading accuracy at low resolution and on held-out reports
links.effect: Low-resolution accuracy rose from 60.0% to 98.5%. Held-out accuracy of the same base model improved by 11.0 points (p = 0.0001).
links.quote: Upscaling the page before recognition was the largest single gain, improving low-resolution accuracy from 60.0% to 98.5% and the held-out accuracy of the same base model by 11.0 points (p = 0.0001).

links.comparator_used: Single reader (recogniser) output used alone, including improvements to the recogniser itself
links.outcome: Detection of corrupted laboratory values on held-out data
links.effect: Agreement between two independently built readers caught 193 of 193 corruptions at a 19.8% review rate. Verification reduced undetected errors more than any improvement to the recogniser itself.
links.quote: Requiring agreement between two independently built readers caught 193 of 193 corruptions on held-out data at a 19.8% review rate.

design_hint: dual-reader consensus verification and image upscaling pre-processing
